column_instructions.RFI Number: Located below the text 'RFI Number'. ignor any additonal latters after the number
column_instructions.RFI Revision Number: Always located at the top, in the left corner, next to the text 'Rev. No' (sometimes printed as 'Rev. N'). Read the digits exactly as printed, then strip every leading zero character until the first non-zero digit is reached — do not remove a zero that is not a leading zero (e.g. '10' stays '10', '203' stays '203'). If the number consists only of zeros, the result must be a single '0' (never an empty string). Apply this normalization consistently on every document. Examples: '000' -> '0', '00' -> '0', '0' -> '0', '01' -> '1', '007' -> '7', '010' -> '10', '002' -> '2', '12' -> '12'.
column_instructions.Discipline: If the document number contains the letter 'C', the discipline is Civil. If it contains the letter 'E', the discipline is Electrical.If it contains the letter 'M', the discipline is Mechanical.
column_instructions.Site Location: Always set this to 'General', written in English only.
column_instructions.WBS Number: Always located below the text 'WBS number'.
column_instructions.ITP reference: Always located below the text 'ITP reference' — extract the number only, without the word 'ITP'.
Found below the text 'Drawings no/ remarks'. Copy every drawing number exactly as written, one per line, keeping the line breaks. A line may be drawn through the text, or the text may touch the cell border: ignore the line and read each letter by its shape (C is open with no inner bar, G has a small horizontal bar inside its opening). Never correct, merge or drop a number.
column_instructions.Description: Extract the text found in the box below 'Item description'.
column_instructions.Result of the Inspection: Look ONLY at Section 20 'Result of the inspection'. Each option has its own checkbox immediately to the LEFT of its label: Approved, Approved with comments, Reschedule, Rejected. Examine every checkbox carefully for a checkmark. A mark can be a tick to the left of, to the right of or under the word, or a circle/oval around the word. If an earlier mark was cancelled (crossed out with an X, a scribble or a line through it), the cancelled mark does not count: ignore it and use the option that carries the remaining valid mark (the last one made); a cancelled mark never makes the result 'more than one marked'. If exactly one checkbox is marked, output only the matching value: Approved -> Accepted, Approved with comments -> Acc. with comments, Reschedule -> Reschedule, Rejected -> Rejected. Never guess or infer a result. If no checkbox is marked (or more than one appears marked), before defaulting to Ongoing inspection you must check Section 21 ONLY: look for any handwritten signature above the word 'Signature' in either of the two signature boxes of Section 21 specifically. Completely IGNORE any handwriting, initials, stamps, or signatures found in the margin at the bottom of the page (the printed strip below Section 21, typically used for document-control or receipt marks) — that area is NEVER part of Section 21 and must never be treated as an approval signature, no matter how similar it looks. Only a signature physically inside one of the two Section 21 signature boxes counts. If such a signature is present there, output 'No approval selected despite signature present' instead. If there is no signature inside those two Section 21 boxes (even if there is handwriting in the bottom margin), output Ongoing inspection.
column_instructions.Comments: Extract the text found in the 'General Comments' section, and ignore any text found in the margin at the bottom of the page.
column_instructions.Engineer Approval Date: Found in Section 21 'Project QHSSE Approval' — this is the LEFT approval box, to the left of Section 22 'PMT Approval'. Read the handwritten date directly above the word 'Signature' in this box only. If that box has only a signature with no handwritten date next to or above it, leave this field empty. Never take a date from Section 22 or from the bottom-margin receive date for this field.
column_instructions.SM Approval Date: Found in Section 22 'PMT Approval' — this is the RIGHT approval box, to the right of Section 21 'Project QHSSE Approval'. Read the handwritten date directly above the word 'Signature' in this box only. This box very often has only a signature with no date of its own: in that specific case, as an intentional exception to the general rule against borrowing values from a neighboring field, use the handwritten date found in Section 21 'Project QHSSE Approval' instead (the same date as Engineer Approval Date). If Section 21 also has no handwritten date, leave this field empty. Never use the bottom-margin receive date for this field.
column_instructions.Remarks: Always leave this column empty — it is filled in automatically after extraction based on the inspection result.
column_instructions.Receive date: The receive date is usually found at the bottom margin of the page, handwritten — typically at the bottom-center, or most often at the bottom-right, physically separate from and below the Section 21/22 signature boxes above it. Do not confuse it with Engineer Approval Date or SM Approval Date. This is an actual completed-event date: it must not be later than the trusted current date and must not be earlier than Inspection Date. Apply these time constraints only to resolve two or more genuinely plausible visual readings of an unclear handwritten digit. Never alter a visually clear date; if a clear date violates a constraint, preserve it and flag a validation conflict for user review.

column_instructions.MIR Number: Located next to the text 'Ref. No'.
column_instructions.MIR Revision Number: Always located at the top, in the left corner, next to the text 'Rev. No' (sometimes printed as 'Rev. N'). Read the digits exactly as printed, then strip every leading zero character until the first non-zero digit is reached — do not remove a zero that is not a leading zero (e.g. '10' stays '10', '203' stays '203'). If the number consists only of zeros, the result must be a single '0' (never an empty string). Apply this normalization consistently on every document. Examples: '000' -> '0', '00' -> '0', '0' -> '0', '01' -> '1', '007' -> '7', '010' -> '10', '002' -> '2', '12' -> '12'.
column_instructions.Inspection Date: Usually the date located in the middle of the page, below the text 'Date'.
column_instructions.Discipline: Look at the position immediately adjacent to 'MIR' in the document number — the discipline letter can appear either right before 'MIR' or right after it, always set off by hyphens on both sides. The discipline is Civil in two cases: if there is no such letter in either of those two adjacent positions at all (e.g. 2028-PSP-PDC-MIR-0000119), or if that letter is 'C' (e.g. 2028-PSP-PDC-MIR-C-000002) — both mean Civil. If there is a single letter immediately before 'MIR' (e.g. 2028-PSP-PDC-E-MIR-000002) or immediately after it (e.g. 2028-PSP-PDC-MIR-E-000002) and it is 'E', the discipline is Electrical. If it is 'M', the discipline is Mechanical. Do not rely on any letter appearing elsewhere in the number — only these two positions directly touching 'MIR' determine the discipline.
column_instructions.Material: The value must always be identical to whatever text you extract for the 'Description of Materials' column (the text next to 'Description of Material'). Do not use the separate line labeled 'Material :' that appears directly under 'Description of Material:' on this form — that specific line is left blank by the preparer on essentially every document and must be ignored completely; never let it cause this column to be empty. Always copy the complete text of the 'Description of Material' field exactly as printed, from its very first word to its very last word — never a shortened or partial version, and never just the shorter general category that appears on the 'Scope of Works' line above it. Never leave this field empty when 'Description of Material' has any visible text.
column_instructions.Description Usage: Located only in the dedicated field labeled 'Description/Usage'. Extract the complete text of this field exactly as printed, from its very first word to its very last word — never a partial or shortened version. On some documents this line's underline is broken or dashed with a visible gap partway through, and the text can appear split into two parts around that gap; if you notice this, still combine both parts into one single value because the gap is only a printing artifact in the underline, not two separate fields. If there is no such gap, simply extract the full text as usual and do not search for a second part that is not there. If the dedicated 'Description/Usage' field is blank or has no readable text, leave this column empty. Never copy, infer, or substitute a value from 'Description of Material', 'Description of Materials', 'Material', or any other field.
column_instructions.Quantity: Located next to the text 'Qty'. Always extract the complete text of this field exactly as printed, from its very first word to its very last word — never a partial or shortened version, and never leave it empty if any text is visible on this line. On some documents this line's underline is broken or dashed with a visible gap partway through (for example a quantity such as '4 Rafters' followed further along the same line by extra text such as a batch number), and the text can appear split into two parts around that gap; if you notice this, still combine both parts into one single value (the gap is only a printing artifact in the underline, not two separate fields). If there is no such gap, simply extract the full text as usual — do not search for a second part that is not there.
column_instructions.Description of Materials: Located next to the text 'Description of Materials'.
column_instructions.Result of the Inspection: Look at the 'PDC's Comments' section, which has exactly three printed options: 'Approved', 'Approved with Comments' and 'Rejected' (an older form may print 'Not Approved' instead of 'Rejected'). Determine the result ONLY from which of these options has a handwritten mark placed on its own word — never decide this from anything else on the page. A mark can be a tick to the left of, to the right of or under the word, or a circle/oval around the word. If an earlier mark was cancelled (crossed out with an X, a scribble or a line through it), the cancelled mark does not count: ignore it and use the option that carries the remaining valid mark (the last one made); a cancelled mark never makes the result 'more than one marked'. Mapping: Approved -> Accepted. Approved with Comments -> Acc. with comments. Rejected (or Not Approved) -> Rejected. If none of the options has a valid mark, the result is 'Ongoing inspection'. Base this decision on the mark alone: completely ignore any handwritten comments, notes, or remarks written anywhere on the page (inside the Comments box or in the bottom margin), even when that text describes rejected, missing, or non-conforming items — that text belongs only in the separate 'Comments' column and must never change the value of this column. Do not mistake unrelated pen marks (such as signatures elsewhere on the page) for this mark.
column_instructions.SEPDC Representatives: If the document number contains the letter 'E', the representative is 'Hamid Altaf'. If it does not contain that letter, the discipline is Civil and the representative is 'Ahmed Din'.
column_instructions.Comments: Ignore any text written in the margin at the bottom of the page. If there is no text in the Comments section itself, leave this field empty.
column_instructions.Status: If the approval type is 'Approved' or 'Accepted', the status is 'Closed'. If it is 'Not Approved' or 'Ongoing inspection', the status is 'Open'.
column_instructions.Engineer Approval Date: Extract the date only from the second-to-last box, and ignore any other dates or text in the margins. If the approval type is 'Ongoing inspection', or if there is no date in that box, leave this field empty. Otherwise this is an actual completed-event date: it must not be later than the trusted current date and must not be earlier than Inspection Date. Apply these time constraints only to resolve two or more genuinely plausible visual readings of an unclear handwritten digit. Never alter a visually clear date; if a clear date violates a constraint, preserve it and flag a validation conflict for user review.
column_instructions.Remarks: Always leave this column empty — it is filled in automatically after extraction based on the inspection result.
column_instructions.Receive date: This field must be searched for visually on every MIR document, even when no spatial highlight is available. Inspect the entire bottom margin of the first page from edge to edge, looking first at the bottom-right and then the bottom-center. The date is normally handwritten and may be outside the printed form border or below the main boxes; do not ignore it merely because it is in the margin. The instruction for the 'Comments' column to ignore bottom-margin text applies ONLY to Comments and must never be applied to Receive date. Do not copy Inspection Date, Engineer Approval Date, the current date, or a file timestamp. If a handwritten receive date is visibly present in the bottom margin, return it; leave this column empty only after carefully checking the complete bottom margin and finding no readable receive date. This is an actual completed-event date: it must not be later than the trusted current date and must not be earlier than Inspection Date. Apply these time constraints only to resolve two or more genuinely plausible visual readings of an unclear handwritten digit. Never alter a visually clear date; if a clear date violates a constraint, preserve it and flag a validation conflict for user review.

template.name: NCR
columns: Drawing No./ Standard / Procedure / Contract violated

The full document number is printed directly under the title 'NON-CONFORMANCE REPORT' at the top centre of page 1, in the form NN-NCR-SCP-XXX-NNN (example: 03-NCR-SCP-ELE-003). Return ONLY the part that comes after 'SCP-', copied verbatim with its hyphen and its leading zeros — from that example return exactly: ELE-003. Do not return the whole number, do not drop the letters, and do not return the digits alone.
column_instructions.Discipline: Derive this from the value you returned for the 'NCR No.' column, not from the body of the document. If it starts with 'ELE' the discipline is Electrical. If it starts with 'CIV' or 'CE' it is Civil. If it starts with 'MEC' or 'ME' it is Mechanical. If it starts with 'PM' it is General. If the prefix is none of these, leave the column empty instead of guessing.
column_instructions.Date Issued: The date printed in the cell to the right of the label 'Issuance Date' in the upper block of page 1. It is often written as a month name with a day and a year (example: JUN 21, 2026.). Return it as DD/MM/YYYY — that example becomes 21/06/2026. Never take any other date on the page here, and in particular never take the NCR Closure date.
column_instructions.Originator/ Person: The person's NAME only, taken from the 'Reported By' row of the table whose header row reads 'This | Name | Position | Signature'. Return the content of the Name cell alone: do not append the Position (such as 'Electrical Engineer') and do not use the 'Validated By' or 'Concurred By' rows.
column_instructions.Area: The text inside the cell to the right of the label 'Part/Item Location' in the upper block of page 1 (example: GSUT HV duct bank). Copy it verbatim. Do not use the 'Part/Item Description' cell, and do not use the OWNER or CONTRACTOR header cells.
column_instructions.Description of NCR: The full text of the section headed 'Description of Non-Conformance' only, copied verbatim and completely, without summarising or rewording. Stop at the end of that box: never include the 'Reported By / Validated By / Concurred By' rows, the ROOT CAUSE section, or the ACTION PLAN section.
column_instructions.Drawing No./ Standard / Procedure / Cont: Read the small table under the heading 'References: Drawing No./ Standard / Procedure / Contract violated'. Its columns are Number, Rev, Title, Section. For every row that actually contains content, return 'Number - Title' (example: CE-300040 - cable raceway site works ITP). Skip completely empty rows, ignore the Rev and Section columns, and if the same Title repeats in more than one row do not repeat it. If more than one filled row remains, separate them with ' | '.
column_instructions.Classification of Non-Conformance: In the section headed 'Classification of Non-conformance (mark with a ✓)' every option has a small checkbox to the LEFT of its label. Return EVERY option whose box carries a visible mark (✓, x, a filled box, or a shaded box) — marking more than one option is normal and common in this form, so never stop at the first one you find. Separate multiple values with ', ' in the order they appear on the page. The only allowed values are exactly: Project Management, Planning and Control, Transportation, Health and Safety, Environmental, Construction, QA/QC, Engineering, Equipment Damage, Owner Complaint, Document Control, Others, Material. An empty box (☐) is NOT selected, and the mere presence of a printed label never means it is selected. If no box in the whole section is marked, leave the column empty.
column_instructions.Non-Conformance Level: Directly under the heading 'NON-CONFORMANCE LEVEL' there are exactly three options, each with a checkbox to the LEFT of its label: Low, Medium, High. Return only the one whose box carries a visible mark (✓, x, a filled box, or a shaded box); normally exactly one of the three is marked. If none of the three is marked, leave the column empty — never infer the level from the severity of the description text.
column_instructions.Cause of Non-Conformance: The full text under the heading 'ROOT CAUSE:' — the band that sits between the 'Concurred By' row and the 'ACTION PLAN:' heading. Copy it verbatim and completely, without summarising. If the ROOT CAUSE band exists but is blank, leave the column empty.
column_instructions.Corrective Action: The full text written to the right of the label 'Proposed Corrective (Remedial) Action', inside the ACTION PLAN section. Copy it verbatim and completely, without summarising. If the cell is blank, leave the column empty.
column_instructions.Preventive Action: The full text written to the right of the label 'Proposed Preventive Action', inside the ACTION PLAN section. Copy it verbatim and completely, without summarising. If the cell is blank, leave the column empty.
column_instructions.Status: Exactly one of two values: Closed or Open. Look only at the cell to the right of the label 'NCR Closure date' near the bottom of page 1; the date in it is usually handwritten. If any readable date is present there, return Closed. If that cell is blank, return Open. Never decide this from signatures, stamps, or the wording of the corrective action.
column_instructions.Date Closed: The date in the cell to the right of the label 'NCR Closure date' near the bottom of page 1. It is usually handwritten and often uses dots as separators (example: 25.06.2026). Return it as DD/MM/YYYY — that example becomes 25/06/2026. Read the digits from the shape of the ink only, and never copy the Issuance Date into this column. If the cell is blank, leave it empty.
column_instructions.Work/Rework/ Rejected: Leave it empty unless the document states one of these three words explicitly as the disposition of the non-conformance. Never infer it from the wording of the corrective or preventive action.
